sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐藏”。

sentences.en: And Decode DC.
sentences.zh: 还有“解码华盛顿”。

sentences.en: It's a special joint episode between my friend here, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 这是我和我身边的朋友罗曼·马尔斯联合制作的一期特别节目。

sentences.en: And my friend, Andrea Seabrook.
sentences.zh: 还有我的朋友安德里亚·西布鲁克。

sentences.en: It's election season, as you know, and Andrea and I found out we had a lot of the same questions
sentences.zh: 正如你们所知，现在正是选举季，安德里亚和我发现我们有很多相同的疑问

sentences.en: about the political events that are everywhere right now.
sentences.zh: 关于现在无处不在的政治事件。

sentences.en: Questions like, how much of a debate or a press conference is genuinely spontaneous?
sentences.zh: 比如这些问题：一场辩论或记者会到底有多少是真正自发进行的？

sentences.en: And how much is pre-planned?
sentences.zh: 又有多少是事先安排好的？

sentences.en: Who designs the theater of politics?
sentences.zh: 究竟是谁在设计政治这出戏码？

sentences.en: Why do speeches and town hall meetings look the way they do?
sentences.zh: 为什么演讲和市政厅会议看起来总是那个样子？

sentences.en: And what message are the campaigns trying to express with their design?
sentences.zh: 竞选团队究竟想通过他们的设计传达什么信息？

sentences.en: To answer some of these questions, we track down two of the most interesting people I've
sentences.zh: 为了解答其中一些问题，我们找到了我聊过的

sentences.en: ever talked to in politics, and we ask them for their secrets.
sentences.zh: 政治界最有趣的两个人，向他们讨教秘密。

sentences.en: Secret number one.
sentences.zh: 秘密一。

sentences.en: Every campaign has a brand.
sentences.zh: 每场竞选都有一个品牌。

sentences.en: This is probably not a huge secret to anyone who's paying close attention, but it's more
sentences.zh: 对于任何密切关注政治的人来说，这可能算不上什么惊天大秘密，但它不仅仅是

sentences.en: than just the politician himself as a brand.
sentences.zh: 把政治家本身当成一个品牌那么简单。

sentences.en: It's an abstraction that floats on top of the human being that's running for office.
sentences.zh: 它是一个漂浮在参选真人表象之上的抽象概念。

sentences.en: So Obama in 2008, it was hope.
sentences.zh: 所以在2008年，奥巴马的品牌是希望。

sentences.en: And for Romney right now, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 而对于现在的罗姆尼，我不知道。

sentences.en: I can't really put my finger on it.
sentences.zh: 我真的说不准。

sentences.en: Romney's brand is like a competent businessman who can bring back jobs.
sentences.zh: 罗姆尼的品牌就像是一个能带来工作机会的精明商人。

sentences.en: That is the message that the campaign is selling.
sentences.zh: 这就是竞选团队正在兜售的信息。

sentences.en: And every detail is arranged to market that brand.
sentences.zh: 每一个细节的安排都是为了推销这个品牌。

sentences.en: The politician's clothes, how he walks, what he says, where he goes,
sentences.zh: 政治家的衣着、走路的姿态、说的话、去的地方、

sentences.en: his sense of humor, his wife, his haircut, his watch.
sentences.zh: 他的幽默感、他的妻子、他的发型、他的手表。

sentences.en: Which brings us to secret number two.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了秘密二。

sentences.en: Every campaign has a team of people who are in charge of making every event fit that brand.
sentences.zh: 每场竞选都有一个团队，负责确保每个活动都符合该品牌。

sentences.en: They're called the advanced team.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为先遣队。

sentences.en: From campaign headquarters, they're given a location, a date, a type of event, and a plane ticket.
sentences.zh: 他们从竞选总部领到一个地点、一个日期、一种活动类型以及一张机票。

sentences.en: Donnie Fowler is a longtime advanced guy.
sentences.zh: 唐尼·福勒是一位资深的先遣队员。

sentences.en: He worked for Bill Clinton, Al Gore, John Kerry, Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 他曾为比尔·克林顿、阿尔·戈尔、约翰·克里、巴拉克·奥巴马工作过。

sentences.en: So he's a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个民主党人。

sentences.en: Yes, very much a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 是的，彻头彻尾的民主党人。

sentences.en: And Fowler says that for every campaign event, there's something you have to have on the stage,
sentences.zh: 福勒说，对于每一场竞选活动，你都必须在舞台上安排某种东西，

sentences.en: but it's a different thing in every place.
sentences.zh: 但在不同的地方，东西是不一样的。

sentences.en: Whether it's the flag or in Iowa, the hay bale or the coal miners standing behind you in Ohio
sentences.zh: 不管是国旗、艾奥瓦州的草垛、俄亥俄州站在你身后的煤矿工人，

sentences.en: or the beach if you're in Florida, the naval yard if you're in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 还是如果你在佛罗里达就是海滩，在弗吉尼亚就是海军造船厂。

sentences.en: So you want local color, you want signs of Americana, and you want real people.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要本土风情，需要美国风情的标志，还需要真实的人。

sentences.en: The key, he says, is making the event look genuine.
sentences.zh: 他说，关键在于让活动看起来真实自然。

sentences.en: The politician look more human and good at relating to regular Americans.
sentences.zh: 让政治家看起来更有人情味，更擅长与普通美国人交流。

sentences.en: So you hit Romney in front of a boardroom with a bunch of white guys in blue suits and red ties.
sentences.zh: 所以你会把罗姆尼安排在一间会议室前，背景是一群穿蓝西装红领带的白人男子。

sentences.en: Because even though his background, to his benefit, to his credit, is from the corporate boardroom,
sentences.zh: 因为尽管他的背景——这对他很有利，也值得肯定——来自企业高层会议室，

sentences.en: that's not the kind of images you want to choose when you're running for president.
sentences.zh: 但当你竞选总统时，那并不是你想选择的形象。

sentences.en: Now, John Seton, a Republican advanced guy, agrees.
sentences.zh: 共和党的先遣队员约翰·西顿对此表示赞同。

sentences.en: Having a bale of hay or a corn reference or something like that certainly kind of gives,
sentences.zh: 摆放一捆干草、玉米或类似的东西，确实能让人

sentences.en: you know, makes it clear that you're somewhere rural.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，清楚地知道你身处某个乡村。

sentences.en: So it makes it clear that, you know, if it's caucus season, you're in Iowa and sends that message.
sentences.zh: 所以这能明确传达出，如果你正处于党团会议季，你就是在艾奥瓦州的信息。

sentences.en: Seton worked for Republicans like John McCain, Sarah Palin, Tim Pawlenty.
sentences.zh: 西顿曾为约翰·麦凯恩、萨拉·佩林、蒂姆·波伦蒂等共和党人工作过。

sentences.en: And that brings us to secret number three.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了秘密三。

sentences.en: The advanced teams run their campaigns pretty much the same way.
sentences.zh: 先遣队运作竞选的方式大同小异。

sentences.en: Some are better funded than others, but they're all doing the same thing,
sentences.zh: 有些资金更充足，但他们都在做同一件事，

sentences.en: marketing their brand day by day, event by event.
sentences.zh: 日复一日、一场接一场地推销他们的品牌。

sentences.en: Fowler says the advanced team flies into the event location a week or more before a speech or rally.
sentences.zh: 福勒说，先遣队在演讲或集会前一周或更早就会飞往活动地点。

sentences.en: A 20-minute event requires several dozen people, campaign staff, secret service.
sentences.zh: 一场20分钟的活动需要几十个人，包括竞选工作人员和特勤人员。

sentences.en: They start there from zero and work hundreds and hundreds of hours to put together
sentences.zh: 他们从零开始，投入成百上千个小时来筹备

sentences.en: what might be that 20-minute campaign stop.
sentences.zh: 可能只有20分钟的竞选停留。

sentences.en: The advanced team is responsible for the staging of the event,
sentences.zh: 先遣队负责活动的布景，

sentences.en: from the flowers to the backdrop to the security and the audience.
sentences.zh: 从鲜花、背景板到安保和观众。

sentences.en: The first big decision is where to have the event.
sentences.zh: 第一个重大决定是活动在哪里举行。

sentences.en: And that, says Fowler, can so easily go wrong.
sentences.zh: 福勒说，而这极容易出错。

sentences.en: Like in 2004, when John Kerry went to the key primary state of South Carolina to announce his candidacy.
sentences.zh: 就像在2004年，约翰·克里前往关键初选州南卡罗来纳州宣布参选。

sentences.en: Kerry's a Vietnam War hero, and he gave his speech before the USS Yorktown, a massive aircraft carrier.
sentences.zh: 克里是越战英雄，他在“约克城号”航空母舰——一艘巨大的航空母舰前发表了演讲。

sentences.en: Which at the time seemed like a good idea.
sentences.zh: 当时这似乎是个好主意。

sentences.en: Everyone in America knows it's not fair.
sentences.zh: 全美都知道这不公平。

sentences.en: The crowd was tiny, and especially in front of a huge aircraft carrier, a tiny crowd looks even tinier.
sentences.zh: 人群非常少，特别是在一艘巨大的航母衬托下，稀少的人群显得更加寥寥无几。

sentences.en: And fair once and for all.
sentences.zh: 彻底求个公正。

sentences.en: There's a big lesson in this one, says Fowler.
sentences.zh: 福勒说，这里面有一个沉重的教训。

sentences.en: Don't put the candidate in a situation where he looks diminished because you can't build a crowd.
sentences.zh: 不要把候选人置于让他显得气势全无的境地，只因为你聚拢不到足够的人气。

sentences.en: Same as the Romney economic speech this year, where he put it in a football stadium
sentences.zh: 就像罗姆尼今年的经济演讲一样，他把它放在一个足球场举行，

sentences.en: and there was only a few thousand people and it looked like nobody showed up to hear Romney talk about the economy.
sentences.zh: 现场只有几千人，看起来就像没人来听罗姆尼谈论经济一样。

sentences.en: I want to thank the folks at the Ford Field for making this space available for us.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢福特球场的朋友们为我们提供这个场地。

sentences.en: I guess we had a hard time finding a large enough place to meet, and this certainly is.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很难找到一个足够大的地方来开会，而这里绝对够大。

sentences.en: Now, the Republican advanced guy, Seton, also talked about that Romney speech.
sentences.zh: 共和党的先遣队员西顿也谈到了罗姆尼的那次演讲。

sentences.en: And he, too, says choosing a venue that's too large can be disastrous.
sentences.zh: 他也认为选择一个过大的场地可能是灾难性的。

sentences.en: You know, immediately before the candidate even takes the stage, you're going to have people tweeting
sentences.zh: 你知道的，甚至在候选人登台之前，就会有人发推特

sentences.en: and blogging about how, you know, Candidate X clearly doesn't have very much support in this county
sentences.zh: 和写博客说，候选人X在这个县明显没有什么支持率，

sentences.en: because his venue is basically empty.
sentences.zh: 因为他的场地基本上是空的。

sentences.en: And then remember, those weak applauses, the camera's pan of the empty stadium,
sentences.zh: 然后记住，那些稀疏的掌声、摄像机扫过空旷体育场的镜头，

sentences.en: will be played over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 会被一遍又一遍地播放。

sentences.en: Romney's campaign couldn't even fill all the chairs in the audience.
sentences.zh: 罗姆尼的竞选团队甚至无法坐满观众席上的所有椅子。

sentences.en: Secret number four is a corollary to this.
sentences.zh: 秘密四是这其中的一个衍生结果。

sentences.en: Every campaign these days sends out, well, spies, I guess you could call them,
sentences.zh: 如今每场竞选都会派出——嗯，你可以称他们为间谍——

sentences.en: to every one of their opponent's events.
sentences.zh: 去到对手的每一场活动中。

sentences.en: In politics, they're called trackers, says Seton.
sentences.zh: 西顿说，在政治上，他们被称为追踪者。

sentences.en: Every event, generally anymore, is going to have trackers from the other campaigns.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，现在每场活动都会有来自其他竞选阵营的追踪者。

sentences.en: You don't want to give them anything to use on the visual side that will hurt your candidate.
sentences.zh: 你绝不想在视觉上给他们任何可以利用来伤害你候选人的把柄。

sentences.en: So here's the half secret.
sentences.zh: 所以半个秘密是这样的。

sentences.en: The advanced staff of one candidate often becomes friendly with the trackers of their opponent.
sentences.zh: 一个候选人的先遣人员往往会和对手的追踪者成为朋友。

sentences.en: Morning, Ralph.
sentences.zh: 早上好，拉尔夫。

sentences.en: Morning, Sam.
sentences.zh: 早上好，萨姆。

sentences.en: I mean, hey, they're in the same line of work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，嘿，他们干的是同一行。

sentences.en: They see each other everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们到处都能见到彼此。

sentences.en: It's their life.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的生活。

sentences.en: Well, uh, better luck next time, Ralph.
sentences.zh: 好吧，祝你下次好运，拉尔夫。

sentences.en: Oh, sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: You can't win them all, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不可能每次都赢。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Nice day, huh, Sam?
sentences.zh: 天气不错，对吧，萨姆？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: Good to be alive, Ralph.
sentences.zh: 活着真好，拉尔夫。

sentences.en: Secret number five.
sentences.zh: 秘密五。

sentences.en: Everything is staged.
sentences.zh: 一切都是安排好的。

sentences.en: I cannot stress this enough.
sentences.zh: 怎么强调这一点都不为过。

sentences.en: And the longer in advance an event is planned, the more granular that staging becomes.
sentences.zh: 一场活动提前筹划的时间越长，这种布景就越发细致入微。

sentences.en: Take the debates, says Fowler.
sentences.zh: 福勒说，以辩论为例。

sentences.en: So what you're seeing is not an extemporaneous debate between two very smart people.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的并不是两个极度聪明的人之间即兴的辩论。

sentences.en: No, it's an incredibly finely staged theater.
sentences.zh: 不，这是一场经过极其精细排练的戏剧。

sentences.en: Every little detail about that stage, how they're standing, is discussed and litigated early.
sentences.zh: 关于那个舞台的每一个微小细节、他们如何站立，都经过了早期的讨论和争论。

sentences.en: And if you watch carefully, says Seton, you can tell.
sentences.zh: 西顿说，如果你仔细观察，就能看出来。

sentences.en: Look at how the candidates shake hands, the presence they have with each other, what they're doing when the other person's talking.
sentences.zh: 看看候选人如何握手、他们在彼此面前的气场、当对方说话时他们在做什么。

sentences.en: Then there are the conventions.
sentences.zh: 还有代表大会。

sentences.en: Also, incredible dramaturgical feats.
sentences.zh: 同样是令人惊叹的戏剧表演壮举。

sentences.en: From the message of the speeches to the timing of the balloon drop.
sentences.zh: 从演讲的内容到气球落下的时间。

sentences.en: Even the chants of the crowds that seem so spontaneous, they're completely pre-planned by the campaign staff.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些看起来如此自发的群众口号，也完全是由竞选工作人员预先策划好的。

sentences.en: Even when people are chanting, they're also kind of part of the production.
sentences.zh: 即使是在喊口号的时候，他们其实也是制作环节的一部分。

sentences.en: Seton says each section of the convention floor has a campaign whip who receives instructions passed down from a central planner.
sentences.zh: 西顿说，大会会场的每一个区域都有一个竞选督导，负责接受从中央规划者那里传达下来的指令。

sentences.en: And the whips then make sure that their sections are chanting appropriately.
sentences.zh: 然后督导们确保他们负责的区域做出恰当的口号呼喊。

sentences.en: Because left to their own devices, a big group can become a big, stupid mob.
sentences.zh: 因为如果听之任之，一大群人就会变成一大群愚蠢的暴民。

sentences.en: Like at the Republican convention this year, when a bunch of people started chanting USA,
sentences.zh: 就像今年共和党全国代表大会上那样，当一群人开始高呼“美国”时，

sentences.en: preventing the committee woman from Puerto Rico from taking the mic.
sentences.zh: 阻止了来自波多黎各的女委员上台发言。

sentences.en: Which actually brings us to secret number six.
sentences.zh: 这实际上将我们带到了秘密六。

sentences.en: No matter how carefully the advance team plans, campaign events can and do go wrong.
sentences.zh: 无论先遣队计划得多么周密，竞选活动还是会出岔子，而且确实经常出岔子。

sentences.en: And the biggest screw-ups, says Seton, are totally self-inflicted.
sentences.zh: 西顿说，最大的失误完全是自找的。

sentences.en: And then I think everyone remembers Governor Palin doing an interview in front of turkeys being killed.
sentences.zh: 然后我想每个人都记得佩林州长在即将被宰杀的火鸡前接受采访。

sentences.en: The event was supposed to be a pardoning of a Thanksgiving turkey, Palin's attempt to do a presidential event.
sentences.zh: 这个活动本该是赦免感恩节火鸡，这是佩林模仿总统规格活动的一次尝试。

sentences.en: But when she took questions from reporters, she stood right in front of a slaughtering table.
sentences.zh: 但当她接受记者提问时，她就站在屠宰台的正前方。

sentences.en: Oh, we didn't get to be invited to participate in this and, you know...
sentences.zh: 哦，我们没有被邀请参与其中，而且，你知道的……

sentences.en: Behind her right now, a man is hoisting live turkeys up into a cone so he can slit their necks and bleed them to death.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，在她身后，一个男人正把活火鸡吊进一个锥形筒里，以便割断它们的喉咙并放血致死。

sentences.en: You see this happening and it's just like, there was no one there to say,
sentences.zh: 你看到这一幕发生，就会觉得，当时怎么会没有人说一句，

sentences.en: wait a minute, maybe we should move this interview, you know, five feet over to the left or something.
sentences.zh: 等一下，也许我们应该把这次采访往左移动个五英尺左右什么的。

sentences.en: Donnie Fowler remembers a fancy fundraiser for Bill Clinton's 1996 re-election campaign.
sentences.zh: 唐尼·福勒还记得为比尔·克林顿1996年连任竞选举办的一场豪华筹款活动。

sentences.en: Harvey Weinstein and Paul Newman were going to introduce President Clinton into this big fundraiser in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 哈维·韦恩斯坦和保罗·纽曼原本要在一个大型康涅狄格州筹款活动上介绍克林顿总统登台。

sentences.en: And I was in charge of telling Paul Newman and Harvey Weinstein when they were going to go up on the stage
sentences.zh: 当时我负责告诉保罗·纽曼和哈维·韦恩斯坦他们什么时候上台

sentences.en: to welcome President Clinton into the room.
sentences.zh: 来迎接克林顿总统进入房间。

sentences.en: And in my little earpiece, I heard, where are you in the program?
sentences.zh: 然后我在小耳机里听到：“你们的流程进行到哪了？”

sentences.en: We're on our way.
sentences.zh: “我们正在过去。”

sentences.en: And so I went to Mr. Weinstein and Mr. Newman and I said,
sentences.zh: 于是我走到韦恩斯坦先生和纽曼先生面前说：

sentences.en: gentlemen, it's time for you to go and introduce President Clinton into the room.
sentences.zh: “先生们，你们该上台去迎接克林顿总统进场了。”

sentences.en: So they stand up and they say how happy they are to be there.
sentences.zh: 于是他们站起来，表达了他们能来到这里的喜悦之情。

sentences.en: And they say, ladies and gentlemen, will you please stand up and welcome President Clinton into the room?
sentences.zh: 他们说：“女士们先生们，请起立，欢迎克林顿总统入场！”

sentences.en: The doors in the back of the room opened, the spotlight shone on the doors, and in walked Kenny G.
sentences.zh: 房间后门打开，聚光灯打在门上，走进来的是肯尼·G（萨克斯演奏家）。

sentences.en: So Harvey Weinstein and Paul Newman looked at me from the stage like, what the heck is going on, man?
sentences.zh: 于是哈维·韦恩斯坦和保罗·纽曼在台上看着我，那表情就像是在问：这到底是怎么回事，老兄？

sentences.en: Fowler realized the wrong person had been talking in his earpiece, saying, let's get started, we're on our way.
sentences.zh: 福勒这才意识到，之前在耳机里说话的人搞错了，对方说的是“我们开始吧，我们在路上了”。

sentences.en: He thought it was Clinton's handlers, but it had been Kenny G's.
sentences.zh: 他以为那是克林顿的随行人员，但其实是肯尼·G的人。

sentences.en: And that brings us to secret number seven.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了秘密七。

sentences.en: Everyone traveling with the campaign, the advance team, the handlers, probably even the candidate, ends up loathing the music.
sentences.zh: 所有随竞选团队旅行的人——先遣队、随员，可能甚至包括候选人——最终都会厌恶这些音乐。

sentences.en: So do the reporters.
sentences.zh: 记者们也是如此。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful day!
sentences.zh: 多么美好的一天！

sentences.en: The sort of upbeat, we love America pop song that every candidate has.
sentences.zh: 那种每个候选人都会有的、乐观向上且充满“我们热爱美国”情调的流行歌曲。

sentences.en: Da-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na.
sentences.zh: 哒啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦啦。

sentences.en: Da-na-da-da-da-na-na-na.
sentences.zh: 哒啦哒哒哒啦啦啦。

sentences.en: God, it just makes me ill.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这真让我觉得恶心。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's rock and roll, sometimes it's country, but it's inevitably an upbeat pop song that you come to the stage and you leave the stage and work the rope line with too.
sentences.zh: 有时是摇滚乐，有时是乡村音乐，但不可避免地，都是一首节奏明快的流行歌曲，你登台、离场，还要在警戒绳边与人群互动。

sentences.en: Brooks and Dunn's got their song, Only in America, that I think has been used by both parties since President Bush in 2004.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克斯和邓恩的歌《Only in America》，我想自2004年布什总统以来，两党都在使用。

sentences.en: The patriotic mix.
sentences.zh: 这种爱国主义拼盘。

sentences.en: Seton and Fowler, both of them, serious political animals, told us they do not miss that in the off years.
sentences.zh: 西顿和福勒两人都是不折不扣的政治动物，他们告诉我们，在非大选年他们并不会怀念这个。

sentences.en: So Seton, Fowler, I can't remember who's the Republican and who's the Democrat.
sentences.zh: 所以，西顿，福勒，我记不清谁是共和党人，谁是民主党人了。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这并不重要。

sentences.en: They're putting on the same show.
sentences.zh: 他们都在上演同一出戏。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Andrea Seabrook, Lino Macitsi, Sam Greenspan, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由安德里亚·西布鲁克、利诺·马西齐、萨姆·格林斯潘以及我——罗曼·马尔斯制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of KALW and the AIA San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是KALW和旧金山美国建筑师学会的项目。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞本节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在Twitter、Instagram和Spotify上。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links, and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但要了解关于这个故事的更多信息，包括精彩的图片和链接，并收听《99% Invisible》的所有单集，请访问99pi.org。
